conviction_note: Management's own Q2 call guide (NIM +2bp, expenses $24.0-24.8M, non-interest income $3.8-4.1M) arithmetically implies Q3 EPS near $1.55-1.58 against a $1.50-1.51 consensus. That is a slight upside lean (p_up 54) on a scale of 3.0, where the median reaction is 2.37 and turnover is thin. This name has beaten 7 of 7 quarters, and its last three modest beats traded -1.4, -3.3 and +0.6, so the beat is the expectation. A Fed hike on 2026-09-16 (the CFO said a hike costs about one quarter of NIM) and a credit-resolution promise that cuts both ways pull the per-finding sum to about zero (-0.1). The two measurements differ in sign only at noise level, and that is the honest read.

findings.finding: Management's own Q2 call guidance implies Q3 EPS of about $1.55-1.58 against the $1.50-1.51 consensus. The guide was NIM up 'a couple basis points' in Q3 from 4.24%, non-interest expense $24.0-24.8M (Q2 $24.6M), non-interest income $3.8-4.1M, and mid-single-digit loan growth on Q2-end loans of $2.78B (+1.9% QoQ). On roughly $3.43B of average earning assets at 4.26% over 92 days, that gives NII near $36.6-36.8M against Q2's $35.8M record, so revenue is about $40.5M against the $40.17M estimate. With provision about $0.8M, tax about 19.5% and about 7.85M diluted shares, EPS lands near $1.56. A 3-6 cent beat is likely, but this bank has beaten EPS 7 of 7 quarters, so a beat is the market's base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats against MarketBeat consensus: Q2 2026 +$0.02 traded +0.63%; Q1 2026 +$0.06 traded -1.39%; Q4 2025 +$0.07 traded -3.26%; Q3 2025 +$0.22 traded +2.37%; Q2 2025 +$0.21 traded +0.62%; Q1 2025 +$0.23 traded +10.66% (April 2025 macro rebound). Beats of 2-7 cents have been flat to sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.50-1.51 sits only 2-3 cents above Q2's $1.48. It does not carry the guided NIM step-up, the extra day and the loan growth, and the revenue estimate of $40.17M is below the guidance arithmetic of about $40.5M. If the market had priced it, the stock would not have drifted 5% below its post-Q2 level and its earnings-AVWAP. But a habitual beater's whisper usually sits above the printed consensus, so part of this is priced.
findings.independence: Peer Home BancShares (HOMB, Arkansas/Texas/Florida) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-14: NIM +2bp to 4.53%, interest-bearing deposit cost down to 2.37% from 2.39%, and September total deposit cost 1.81% below the 1.83% quarterly average (https://finviz.com/news/402737/home-bancshares-reports-record-third-quarter-net-income-bringing-the-company-closer-to-a-half-billion-dollar-year). That is a proxy consistent with the guided NIM step-up. The Q2 release itself (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001436425/000162828026048827/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm) supplies the base figures, and the guidance comes from the same company.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0). On the Q2 call, HBCP's CFO said that in a rate-hike scenario NIM is sustained or improved after 'a brief dip of about a quarter when deposit rates rise'. He had also guided NIM expansion 'a little bit into Q4'. So the forward NIM commentary on the 10-20 call risks a Q4 dip or a flatter path, even though Q3 itself saw only two weeks of the hike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history: HBCP gives no formal NIM guide, and the NIM step-ups of Q1/Q2 2026 came with -1.39% and +0.63% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public and sector-wide, so most of it is priced in bank multiples. What is not public is HBCP's own Q4 NIM read after the hike. If that were priced, the 2026-07-21 'a little bit into Q4' expansion would already have been marked down in estimates, and the Q3 revenue estimate ($40.17M) suggests it partly has been.
findings.independence: The CFO's rate-sensitivity statement is in the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15267258756637696). Against it, peer HOMB's September deposit cost still fell to 1.81% after the hike (https://finviz.com/news/402737/home-bancshares-reports-record-third-quarter-net-income-bringing-the-company-closer-to-a-half-billion-dollar-year), so the dip may be small. That is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: Credit is the swing line. At June 30, criticized loans rose to $95.8M (3.45% of loans), NPAs were $39.2M (1.09% of assets), and foreclosed assets/OREO jumped to $12.8M from $4.1M, with foreclosed-asset costs up $331K QoQ. On the Q2 call management promised more than $30M of special-asset improvement by year-end, including about $22M of special-mention resolutions with more than half in Q3, and 14 loans (about one-third of classified) off the balance sheet by year-end. Q3 will show whether criticized loans fell, at what loss, and what OREO write-downs cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NPAs rose from 0.73% of assets in Q2 2025 to about 1.1% in 2026. The prints over that span traded -3.26% (Q4 2025), -1.39% (Q1 2026) and +0.63% (Q2 2026, when NPAs dipped slightly). No print isolates credit as the cause.
findings.why_not_priced: The promise is public, so delivery is priced as likely. What is not priced is the loss content of the resolutions and any OREO marks. If a credit miss were priced, the stock would sit near tangible book ($47.02) rather than at 1.4x; if clean delivery were priced, it would not trade 5% below its post-Q2 level. Asymmetry: in small banks a credit disappointment is punished more than a resolution is rewarded, hence the slight negative.
findings.independence: Peer HOMB's Q3 2026 showed NPLs up to 1.19% of loans from 1.08%, though with lower charge-offs (https://finviz.com/news/402737/home-bancshares-reports-record-third-quarter-net-income-bringing-the-company-closer-to-a-half-billion-dollar-year). That is a regional proxy, not HBCP's book. The HBCP figures come from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001436425/000162828026048827/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm), which shares a source with finding 1.

findings.finding: Loan growth risk. Management called the pipeline 'consistent' but 'not robust', guided only mid-single-digit growth for H2, expects construction balances to keep falling, and warned that problem-loan resolutions would reduce balances. Peer Home BancShares reported an organic community-bank loan decline of about $256M in Q3 2026. A flat-to-low loan quarter would undercut the NII step-up in finding 1 and the 2027 margin narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 loans +7% annualized traded +0.63%. No miss on loans in the baseline window to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: Loan growth is not in the EPS consensus as a separate line. The revenue estimate of $40.17M is conservative enough to absorb some of it, which is why this is sized small. The peer read-through landed on 2026-10-14, after HBCP last spoke, and it is from a different footprint.
findings.independence: HOMB Q3 2026 release (https://finviz.com/news/402737/home-bancshares-reports-record-third-quarter-net-income-bringing-the-company-closer-to-a-half-billion-dollar-year): total loans down $216.6M, loan yield down 5bp. This is a proxy from Arkansas/Texas/Florida, not Acadiana or Houston. Shares the call transcript with findings 1-3.

The stock has since fallen from $71.68 (insider sale price on 2026-08-18) back to about $66, the Q2 repurchase price, while TBV/share was $47.02 and capital was being held as M&A 'dry powder'. The Q3 release may show resumed repurchases or signal them.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): cut the guidance-implied beat from +0.8 to +0.6, because this name's last 2-7 cent beats traded -1.39%, -3.26% and +0.63%. p_up was left at 54, since it was already set with that history in mind.
